items.title: 13 Investment Must Reads for This Week (Aug. 18, 2026)
items.summary: Charles Schwab is looking to hire a director to lead the firm’s long-short SMA platform. Morgan Stanley has beefed up its UMA program to allow a wider variety of assets, including some private market funds. These are among the investment must reads for financial advisors this week.

items.title: Stocks Take Hit as Bond Selloff Saps Risk Appetite
items.summary: A selloff in chipmakers sent stocks lower, with the market also falling as inflation angst and rising government debt kept bond yields elevated. Longer-dated bonds are at the epicenter of anxiety about everything from inflation to the debt-laden artificial-intelligence boom. Liz Ann Sonders, Chief Investment Strategist at Charles Schwab, discusses the gap between sell-side consensus and buy-side expectations.

items.title: SCHW's July 2026 Client Assets Rise Y/Y: A Revenue Growth Signal?
items.summary: Schwab's July client assets rise 19% y/y to $13.04T, while higher net new assets and trading activity point to revenue growth.

items.title: Schwab on the Hunt for Long-Short Strategies Director
items.summary: Charles Schwab has recently been on the search for a director to lead the firm’s long-short separately managed account initiative, someone responsible for building a team focused specifically on long-short SMAs and creating companywide coordination for the business, according to a job posting.  Schwab did not respond to questions, including if the position has been filled.  The move speaks to a broader push into the strategies, which are gaining traction as wealthy investors look for ways to diversify concentrated stock positions without triggering massive tax bills.
